## tools/gloss-store-v1.mjs

### The sign predicate
These three lines stand between markers: from the line opening `const STRONG_SIGN = ` to the line `// end of Strong's sign (tools/gloss-store-v1.mjs)`. The page copies them but for `export`; a check lifts both copies with K2's method.
- `STRONG_SIGN = /^(X|×|\+) /u` — the source-signs ledger's pattern, the page's SOURCE_SIGN[0] byte for byte.
- `STRONG_SIGN_ALONE = /^\(\s*(X|×|\+)\s*\)/u` — the sign held alone in a round bracket at the head of a rendering (the lead's call 1; the M14 declaration's open_paren.holds_sign_alone).
- `opensWithStrongSign(t) -> boolean` — `String(t ?? "")` tested against either pattern.
  - true: «X after», «(+) archer», «(X) very», «(×) very.», «(+)valiant(-ly)».
  - false: «(X great) delight», «Xerxes», a bare «X».

### Opening the store
`openRouteStore(storeDir, { atRest = false, signLast = false })`
- Returns everything it returned before, plus `signLast` (a boolean).
- A `signLast` that is not a boolean is refused (throws).
- With `signLast: true`, `readingPool(routes, order, corpusOf, omit)` makes the sign the first key of all three comparators:
  - oldest: `signed || byOldest`;
  - characters: `signed || ledger || byOldest || at`;
  - corpus: `signed || corpus || byOldest`.
  - `signed(a, b) = Number(opensWithStrongSign(a.text)) - Number(opensWithStrongSign(b.text))`.
  - It is a sort, not a filter: a pool all signed or all plain is unchanged, and the entries' fields are as before.
- Without it, every pool is byte for byte 0b8d555d12's.
- `glossFor`, `tableFor` and every leader drawn from `readingPool` follow with no other edit.

### Rule id, text and stamp
- `GLOSS_RULE_ID = "zone-gloss-rule-v8-printed-form-ledger-division-whole-without-a-ledger-at-rest-a-rendering-carrying-strongs-sign-after-every-plain-one-antiquity-1940-lastuary"`. `GLOSS_RULE_TEXT` gains the sign clause.
- `SIGNS_REST_LAST_RULING` — a string: the lead's calls 1 to 3.
- `signsRestLastStamp(kindsRec) -> { rule: GLOSS_RULE_ID, scope: "data/dictionary-kinds-v1.json scope: " + kindsRec.scope.say, ruling: SIGNS_REST_LAST_RULING }`. It throws if given no record with a scope.
- The intended use by a bake:
  ```js
  const atRest = restsOffIn(kinds.rec, zone);
  openRouteStore(dir, { atRest, signLast: atRest });
  // on such a zone, and on its lattice sidecar:
  emitted_from.signs_rest_last = signsRestLastStamp(kinds.rec);
  ```

### The facts slot
- `FACTS_WRITTEN_BY` (frozen) maps each fact key to the store-index key under which the tool that writes it records its run:
  `{ n: "row_entries", t: "row_entries", b: "row_entries", name: "name_rows", opens: "sense_openings", collocations: "ubs_collocations", picked_at: "ubs_collocations" }`.
- `setFacts(row, facts)` throws on a key `FACTS_WRITTEN_BY` does not name.
- The FACTS_SLOT doc now describes `collocations` (UBS's collocations byte for byte) and `picked_at` (places as `"<book slug> <c>:<v>:<w>"`, e.g. «i-samuel 6:10:15»).

## tools/dictionary-kinds-v1.mjs
- `restsOffOf(rec, mSources, factsOf) -> rule(row, place = null) -> entry | null`.
  - `place` is a string in the picked_at format, or null; anything else throws.
  - An entry with `stands_at` passes over a row when `Array.isArray(factsOf(row)[e.stands_at])` and that list includes `place`. The next entry in the record's order is then asked.
  - The bakes call with no place, so the line never reads such a row.
  - `reads` = `["id", "say", "kinds", "families", "fact", "is", "has", "stands_at", "ruling"]`; any other field is refused.
  - Also refused: a `stands_at` that is not a non-empty string, and a `stands_at` beside no `fact`.
- `restsOffIds(rec, mSources)` is unchanged; M18 is not shut whole.
- The page's copy in zone.html is the module's, line for line.

## tools/row-strikes-follow-v1.mjs
- `ROW_FOLLOW_RULE_ID = "row-strikes-follow-rule-v2-a-name-read-at-an-older-store-is-followed-through-the-rounds-since-and-never-guessed-a-retexted-row-is-followed-to-its-new-words"`.
- `follower({ record, index, readAt })` returns `{ readAt, rounds, nowOf, thenOf, gone, landed, rekeyed, retexted }`.
- New answer from `nowOf(name)` and `thenOf(name)`: `{ state: "retexted", name, text, was, by }`.
  - `name` is `[key, rank, m, sha16Of(newRouteText)]` for `nowOf`; the old name for `thenOf`.
  - `text` is the new route text: slot 1 as served, closes not taken out.
  - `was` is the route text the name was read with.
- New list `retexted`: `[{ name (as read), now, text, was, by }]`.
- Refused (FollowFault):
  - a retext that carries `folded_into`;
  - a retext whose `to_text` is empty or not a string;
  - a row both re-keyed and retexted since.
- The record row the follower reads, as strike-rows writes it today: `{ action: "retext", key, rank, m, route: old text, row: old row whole, to_text: new slot-1 text, from_slot }`. strike-rows v7 must write the same; `"words_back"` is the new from_slot.
- `followedRecord(f, { left, rekeyed, retexted = [], landed })` adds `rows_retexted_and_followed: { <list file>: n }` only where `retexted` is non-empty. `followedSaid` says "N retexted by <list>".

- placeOf(word) gives "<book slug> <c:v:w>", the walk dfltPlaceSaid makes, factored out (dfltPlaces).
- The card names its place once: the open word's, for its own key and its pieces' keys. A run's card and a sidecar word name none. It passes the place to poolFor as opts.kindsAt.
- shutAway, both kinds counts, the welded pair card's count, kindPick and the dotted edge all ask restsOff(row, place).

- A pill whose rows carry the fact says so in its title, in the record's words: «a reading that the UBS dictionary gives under a collocation: …».

(2) The sign.
- The module's block (STRONG_SIGN, STRONG_SIGN_ALONE, opensWithStrongSign, end marker) is copied but for "export". SOURCE_SIGN[0] is STRONG_SIGN, byte for byte the ledger's.
- signsLastOn(bin) reads the zone's own stamp. poolFor sets it on the pool from opts.bin || zone, and carryWithheld, drawPills' copy and the pair's weld keep it.
- sortPool's signLast sits in the same place in the chain, after the license class. On a book of the scope it puts Strong's sign after every plain reading in every position. Under «below» the ledger's other signs come between the plain readings and Strong's.
- The comment and the rail line say what each position does.

(3) Call 4.
- DFLT_STEP_STANDS reads [n, words, 1]. stepOwn stands at those places, or where today's line is bare.
- A stands pair, under STEP, backs the read half with STEP's words: kqPlace, kqPickG's branch path, and the card's read half (placeOfCell).

- The chip, the STEP pill's title, the rail's line and the note above the default sources now say where STEP's words stand.

(4) Call 3.
- runReadsItsWords sits beside runTakesDefault. The span branch, the whole-form branch and chainReadsWhole ask it.
- The run card opens on the as-written rung only where the line reads the run whole.

(5) Question 12.
- The fold runs in poolFor, on a card's pool only (opts.pills), once FORM_OF is here.
- The pill prints formOfSays, with several pointers in one bracket. It carries data-by (every carrier), data-pointer and data-pointer-by. The record shows the reading's own rows first.
- The pill answers to the pointer's raw text and to its printed form (the alias). The kinds count treats that alias as a reading that stands.
- A card drawn before the map lands is rebuilt once the reader's hand is off it.

findings.title: Question 10's exception fails on a word of a named run that call 3 now reads word by word
